samples.summary: New `assertNoDotSegments` guard in `printDryRun` is not exercised by any test — the dry-run tests that claim to cover it pass through `seg()` instead
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/test/dry-run.test.ts:97-111` are the only tests for the refusal. Both drive `sheets cells batch`, and `packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:137` already applies `seg(docId)`/`seg(tab)` before calling `printDryRun`, so `seg()` throws first; the workspace case (test line 105) is caught by `seg(config.workspace)` at dry-run.ts:29. I grepped every `printDryRun(` call site (cells, tabs, docs, notes, slides, files, sheets-import) — all interpolate ids via `seg()`, so no caller can hand `printDryRun` a raw `.`/`..` segment. Deleting `assertNoDotSegments` entirely leaves all four dry-run tests green: the guard ships with coverage that cannot fail for it.

samples.summary: The query-string exemption in `assertNoDotSegments` (`path.split('?')[0]`) has no test
samples.evidence: No dry-run call site currently passes a path containing `?` (grep of `printDryRun(` shows none), and no test in packages/cli/test passes a query to `printDryRun`. A regression that dropped the `split('?')` (or, conversely, one that made a `?range=..` value throw) would not be caught.

samples.summary: `MAX_UPSTREAM_CODE` (80-char truncation of upstream `error.code`) is introduced with no test
samples.evidence: upstream-error.test.ts covers the message cap (line 130), the sibling-drop cap (line 139) and the HTML-message rejection (line 152), but grep for `repeat(`/`MAX_UPSTREAM` across packages/cli/test finds no case with an over-long `code`. Removing the `.slice(0, MAX_UPSTREAM_CODE)` at formatter.ts:162 breaks nothing in the suite.

samples.summary: Dot-segment refusal is only tested at a call site whose dry-run branch sits inside a try/catch; the many dry-run branches that throw outside one are untested
samples.evidence: The test header (dry-run.test.ts:11-17) explicitly picks `cells batch` because its dry-run branch is inside the handler's try/catch. Every other dry-run site — cells.ts:52 (`set`), cells.ts:85 (`delete`), docs.ts:135/155, notes.ts:95/115, slides.ts:100/120, files.ts:64/124/144, tabs.ts:49/78, sheets-import.ts:85 — calls `seg()` outside any try, so a `..` id there escapes the action and depends on `runCli`'s last-resort catch (src/cli.ts:75-77) for the envelope. Nothing in the suite drives that combination, and this test bypasses `runCli` entirely.
searchedFor: grep printDryRun( with context in packages/cli/src/commands

samples.summary: No test asserts the `?range=` query survives the `seg()` refactor of `getCells`, nor that `/files/<id>` download encodes its id
samples.evidence: The `request paths pin every id to one segment` suite (upstream-error.test.ts) only inspects `deleteDocument`, `setCell`, `renameTab` and `listDocuments`. grep for `range=` / `getCells(` across packages/cli/test returns no matches, so the rewritten `getCells` URL (query concatenation) and the rewritten `downloadFileDocument` URL (`/files/${seg(docId)}`) have no URL-level assertion.
searchedFor: read the 'request paths pin every id' describe block in upstream-error.test.ts

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `assertNoDotSegments` exists (dry-run.ts:26, 44-52) but no test can make it throw. The test at dry-run.test.ts:97-103 passes '..' as doc-id, and cells.ts:137 evaluates `seg(docId)` in the template literal before `printDryRun` is called, so url.ts:25-27 throws first with the same 'Invalid path segment' message. The test at dry-run.test.ts:105-111 uses path `/documents/doc-1/tabs/tab-1/cells`, which contains no dot segment, so the guard passes and the throw comes from `seg(config.workspace)` at dry-run.ts:29 — after the guard. Both tests assert only empty stdout / stderr substring / exitCode 1, which hold identically whether the guard exists or not. I checked every printDryRun call site (cells.ts:53,86,134; slides.ts:66,100,120,149,200; tabs.ts:49,78; sheets-import.ts:85; docs.ts:104,135,155,188,243; notes.ts:61,95,115; files.ts:64,124,144) — all interpolate ids via seg(), so no command path reaches the guard. Grepping packages/cli/test for printDryRun / dry-run.js / 'Invalid path segment' finds only dry-run.test.ts:101,109 and upstream-error.test.ts:555-557 (which exercises HttpClient/seg, not printDryRun); no test imports dry-run.ts directly. So the new guard ships with tests that are presented as its coverage but cannot fail for it — fake coverage / missing test for a new behavior, major under the test-adequacy rubric.
